chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then wore a shirt before entering the state of Ihram. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His bath has been broken.'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: Does wearing a shirt before entering Ihram invalidate the ritual bath taken for it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the ritual bath for Ihram is not merely a physical cleansing but a state-bound act; thus, donning clothing before the formal declaration of Ihram invalidates the ghusl. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise timing and intentionality of ritual purity acts, distinguishing between general purification and the specific preparatory rite for the pilgrimage state. It highlights the importance of maintaining the continuity of the ritual act until the specific condition (entering Ihram) is met.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who washes for his Ihraam, then wears a shirt before he wears Ihraam. Heasws said: ‘It breaks his washing (for the Ihraam)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and al-Husayn from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who takes Ghusl (bath) for Ihram, then puts on his shirt before assuming the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘His Ghusl (bath) has become invalid.’”
